merger_name: Apax Funds – Techoraco Limited and Institutional Investor LLC
merger_description:
Assemble UK Bidco Limited and Assemble US Bidco Inc (the **Acquirers**) propose to acquire 100% of the issued share capital of Techoraco Limited (**Techoraco**) and Institutional Investor LLC (**Institutional Investor**) (together, the **Targets**) from Delinian Limited (the **Acquisition**).

The Targets will be acquired as a single business that will be wholly owned by Assemble Midco Limited. Upon completion, the Acquirers intend to operate the Targets as a single business.

The Acquirers are special purpose vehicles which are wholly owned by Assemble Midco Limited, a UK holding company that is ultimately owned by investment funds advised by Apax Partners LLP (**Apax**). Apax is a UK limited liability partnership based in London, UK, and the parent company of a number of entities which provide investment advisory services to private equity funds investing in a range of industry sectors (the **AP Funds**).

Delinian Limited owns a portfolio of companies that provide data, insights, accreditation, and events in select global markets. Relevantly to the Acquisition:

* Techoraco is a business-to-business (**B2B**) in-person events and insights business focussed on the digital infrastructure sector, including data centres, fixed connectivity, wireless and satellite connectivity, and related software and hardware infrastructure.
* Institutional Investor is a B2B membership, in-person events and market intelligence business focussed on the institutional investment sector, including by connecting asset managers and allocators.

The Targets do not have a local presence, office, or employees in Australia, and do not organise events in Australia. They have less than 10 Australian corporate customers who subscribe to the Targets' services and/or attend the Targets' events which take place outside of Australia.

determination_table_content.details:
Assemble UK Bidco Limited and Assemble US Bidco Inc (the
Acquirers) applied for a notification waiver in respect of their
proposed acquisition of 100% of the issued share capital of
Techoraco Limited (Techoraco) and Institutional Investor LLC
(Institutional Investor) (together, the Targets), as described in the
transaction documents provided as part of the application (the
Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The Acquirers are special purpose vehicles which are wholly owned
by Assemble Midco Limited, a UK holding company that is ultimately
owned by investment funds advised by Apax Partners LLP (Apax).
Apax is a UK limited liability partnership based in London, and the
parent company of a number of entities which provide investment
advisory services to private equity funds in a range of industry
sectors (the AP Funds).
Techoraco is a business-to-business (B2B) in-person events and
insights business focussed on the digital infrastructure sector,
including data centres, fixed connectivity, wireless and satellite
connectivity, and related software and hardware infrastructure.
Institutional Investor is a B2B membership, in-person events and
market intelligence business focussed on the institutional
investment sector, including by connecting asset managers and
allocators.
The Targets do not have a local presence, office, or employees in
Australia, and do not organise events in Australia. They have less
than 10 Australian corporate customers who subscribe to the
Targets’ services and/or attend the Targets’ events which take place
outside of Australia.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. The Targets have a small Australian presence and there
is no horizontal overlap or vertical relationship between Apax
(including its connected entities and the AP Funds’ controlled
portfolio companies) and the Targets in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition. There is no horizontal overlap or vertical relationship
between the Targets and any of the AP Funds’ controlled portfolio
companies that are active in Australia.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
